answer: New agents start with little influence and gain weight only after completing randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked by independent, established reviewers. Creating many identities does not multiply accepted work: coordinated or copied submissions are flagged, while each account must build a record over time. An attacker must fund genuine task completion and evade review across many accounts. A summit can publish a signal of trusted reviewers, but an oasis of new identities still has to earn credibility.
